subject: FastPay — inference economics recap & proposed pilot
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FastPay — inference economics recap & proposed pilot

Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I’ve attached a short proposal and the small traffic sample you suggested we use for cost modeling.

Key pain points you called out:
- High per-customer inference costs with peaks on transaction hours (evening PST) that blow past budget.
- Long tail of short, chatty prompts (auth flows, merchant inquiries) where tokens spike.
- Need predictable unit economics to make a go/no-go decision for Q3 product launch.

Goals we discussed:
- Target production TCO <= $25k/month for the initial payments fraud assistant workload (pilot traffic profile in attached CSV).
- Maintain response latency under 300ms p50 and <800ms p95 for interactive flows.
- Proof points: 6-week pilot that demonstrates 2x–3x cost reduction levers in practice (batching, prefix caching, model quantization) without degrading NPS.

Token economics baseline (quick back-of-envelope from the call):
- Current average prompt+completion: ~420 tokens/session, 18k sessions/day peak (from your sample).
- Baseline monthly token consumption ~230M tokens.
- Naive hosted TCO estimate (no batching/caching) exceeds your $25k target by ~2.5x.

Redwood levers we recommend during pilot (these are practical, measurable):
1) Continuous batching for background/async traffic (expected 20–40% token cost reduction on those paths).
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated merchant queries (we’ve seen 30–60% token reuse depending on prompt duplication).
3) Quantized model variant (4-bit) for low-latency scoring paths that are tolerant to small quality change — ~25–35% lower per-token GPU cost.
4) Dynamic routing: route low-risk, high-volume requests to cheaper model variants and reserve higher-capacity models for risk-sensitive flows.

Proposed pilot (6 weeks):
- Week 0: Share sample traffic + create a small private deployment (dedicated pool, feature flags for batching/caching).
- Weeks 1–3: Run mirrored traffic in shadow mode + calibrate batching/caching heuristics.
- Weeks 4–6: Move subset of production traffic (10–25%) with circuit-breaker thresholds; collect cost, latency, and quality metrics.

Deliverables we’ll produce:
- Weekly TCO dashboard (tokens, cost per path, latency percentiles).
- Change log of batching/cache rules and model variants used.
- Final pilot readout with recommended steady-state config and expected monthly cost range.

Immediate asks from FastPay to get started:
- A representative 48–72h request log (anonymized) or the sample CSV you emailed (great start).
- Confirmation of the $25k/mo budget cap for pilot acceptance criteria.
- A SOC2 / procurement contact so we can share security docs.

If that matches what you heard, I’ll loop in our infra engineer to schedule a 30–45m kickoff next week and send the formal pilot SOW.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Thanks, Evelyn — that matches our read. A couple clarifications from my side: we are comfortable with a 6-week pilot but the hard constraint for sign-off is the $25k/month expected steady-state TCO for the pilot scope you outlined. If your final readout shows >$25k with no clear plan to get under that, we can’t proceed to commit resources for the Q3 launch.

On the security side: please send SOC2 Type II and any encryption/KMS docs to procurement@fastpay.com. Our procurement lead (cc’d) will handle the vendor packet.

Also, we can provide a 72h anonymized request log next business day — I’ll pull that and drop it in the Drive link you shared.

Appreciate the clear levers — curious to see the modeled impact once you run the sample through Redwood Optimize.

— Alex

Subject: Re: FastPay — inference economics recap & proposed pilot

Alex — hi, quick technical add from the post-call notes and what we’ll measure in week 1 when we run the traffic sample through our cost model.

What we’ll instrument and report (weekly):
- Token distribution heatmaps (per-route and per-customer).
- Batching efficiency (tokens saved vs ideal/max batch) and its latency impact.
- Cache hit rate on prefix/KV caches and effective token reuse percent.
- Model variant mix (quantized vs full-fp) and per-token GPU cost delta.

Reasonable conservative assumptions I’ll start the model with (we can tighten these after seeing your 72h sample):
- 25% of sessions are cacheable with median token reuse ~45% (conservative).
- Shadow batching across background flows yields 30% token amortization for those paths.
- Quantized 4-bit for scoring reduces GPU cost by 28% while keeping automated quality metrics within acceptable bounds for fraud scoring.

On latency: batching for user-interactive flows will be conservative — we will only batch where we can guarantee p95 < 800ms. For async/nearline jobs we’ll apply aggressive batching.

Next step from a technical side: please upload the anonymized 72h request log and a simple mapping of request_type -> business priority (low/med/high) so we can create routing rules. I’ll run a preliminary cost model and share a one-pager with expected monthly ranges: pessimistic / likely / optimistic.

Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 19:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FastPay pilot pricing options & next steps

Internal note — quick summary of proposed pricing constructs to surface to Alex once Marissa shares the modeled ranges:
1) Commitment-based discounted rate: FastPay signs a 3-month reserved commit for Dedicated capacity. Discount tiers at 30/50/70k commit levels. Useful if they want predictable monthly TCO; reduces unit price but requires commit.
2) Pilot usage cap + overage: Pilot runs on Hosted with a hard billing cap set at $25k/mo for acceptance. Overage allowed with prior approval and a pre-agreed escalation path. Good if they need low friction to start.
3) Hybrid: Dedicated baseline for peak throughput (commit sized to expected 95th percentile) + burst to Hosted for spikes. Middle ground for predictable performance during peak payments windows.

Action items (Evelyn): present the modeled pessimistic/likely/optimistic ranges and propose either (a) pilot-on-hosted with $25k cap or (b) 3-month small commit option.
(Action: Marissa) — run the sample through Redwood Optimize today and share model by end of day tomorrow.
(Action: Dev) — prepare a short SOW template and procurement checklist for FastPay procurement team.

I’ll be on the kickoff call once Alex confirms availability next week.

— Dev
